ratings.comment: Steele knows his literature, however, his lectures are very dull as he just stands in front of podium and speaks for 50 minutes in monotone.  There is a LOT of reading in this course (8 novels) so you have to keep up and not fall behind.  The material is not hard, however, the TA's grade everything and your grade is based on 2 papers, midterm, exam

Professor Steele was one of the best teachers Ive ever had. He gave very interesting insight for all of the books we read. You don't have to read the books but it helps when you follow along in lecture.

8 books. If you expect to keep up with the reading, you're likely to read 30+pages a day. Lectures are pointless: the professor just rambles, not helping with papers or tests. Grade determined by a few assignments; if you do bad on one, you likely get a bad grade. Very little writing practice along with poor instructions on papers and tests.

Would not recommend Prof. Steele. He's conceited, and arrogant. He does care deeply about the material, but the 8 books you read for the class are terrible. He uses the same 2 words all the time, and it will get annoying by the 2nd week. The 2 papers are fairly basic, and exams are long. Expects you to put his class before all else. Avoid the class

Professor Steele is very knowledgable and you can tell he loves the topics discussed in class. There are two 4-6 page papers and 2 exams. The books are actually very interesting. For A's on papers and the exams, try to go beyond the ideas discussed in class. That is what they are looking for! Also go heavy on analysis rather than summary for A's!

This man loves reading and loves ethnic studies. There are two essays both 4-6 pages and 2 exams. The exams are very hard to study for though and your hand will hurt after writing one (3 short essays and 1 long essay in 50 minutes). It is necessary to read the books which tend to be very entertaining to read so it is not terrible.

Professor Steele is an extremely smart man that mainly lectures on the important aspects of the books and makes many of the concepts easier to understand. However, if this class isn't required for your major or you're not insanely passionate about reading, I wouldn't take it. It is a ton of reading and the books (in my opinion) were not the best.

Horrible class. Lectures are just 50 minutes of him rambling and saying things that don't really make much sense. Exams are impossible to complete in the time allowed. Both papers were scheduled within two weeks of each other at the end of the semester. Impossible to get a well deserved grade. TA said she loved my paper, but gave me a B anyways.

Professor Steele is very knowledgable, however his lectures can sometimes get very boring. The nice thing is he tells his TAs to grade easier than they might themselves for an intro class so the class wasn't too hard overall.

He is tough. The man is a genius and the material is fun if you like reading. But he expects next to perfection from students. He tells his TAs that if a student's paper isn't above the TA's level, they cannot earn an A on that paper. Most TAs don't follow that, but it just shows that he is hard. Good lectures, but don't mess around with him.

Really excellent professor. Knows a ton of information and explains things well. and made a pretty "meh" subject to me (New York in the 19th century) fascinating. Also, if you miss a class (which I suggest you don't because lecturers are very useful) he records them for you and posts them online. However, there is A LOT of reading (200 pgs/wk)
He is a natural teacher. Just amazing!
great professor, take good notes and you'll pass easily

Lectures aren't extremely exciting, but if you take notes you will get an A. Usually records his lectures and puts them online. His lectures are to the point and give all the info you need for papers and tests.

Have to read 8 books, all pretty average. 1 midterm and a final, w/ short essay quote ID's and a long essay on theme. Pretty easy if you read the books (or at least SparkNote). Two papers, knocked them out in a couple hours and got A's on both, but my TA was a pretty easy grader. Not the most interesting Comm B, tons of reading, but easy grading.

Prof Steele holds lecture biweekly. Discussion is mandatory and is a decent portion of your grade. Books are interesting and tests are fair. Get a hold of the reading list and finish a few books early. Enjoy! (Also, try to get TA Heather Swan, she's the coolest!)

Prof Steele is a very committed professor. He really cares about the material, and makes the reading more tolerable. He records his lectures, & puts them online. There is quite a bit of reading in this class, and he explains it so well, you might not have to read. Be prepared to read and write. JS is a good prof, and I would recommend him!

I love this guy!  He can be very socially awkward, but he cares a lot about the people who go through his courses.  (I think professors with kids who have been to college are usually way nicer in that way.)  And he really, really knows his stuff when he's talking about the areas he works in.

Steele is hands down one of my favorite professors ever. He is passionate about everything he teaches and makes the most boring reading completely interesting. TAKE HIS CLASSES. He also adds in personal anecdotes that are hilarious and plays awesome music before class. love love love him. genius.

His lectures were pretty boring & useless. He believes in high attendance though, so you have to go to discussion. My TA wasn't the best, but overall the class is relatively easy. You'll have to read 8 books total. There are two exams, the midterm & final. Both exams involve multipe short essays & one long essay.

You can skip lecture, but the discussion has mandatory attendance. It's A LOT of reading. By no means is this a challenging class. Lecture gets very tedious sometimes, though he's an enthusiastic guy and loves what he teaches, and teaches well--it is, however, really a lecture. He talks. For 50 minutes.

Prof. Steele is in my eyes, a complete genius. I can see why in the lower-level English classes he may not seem as awesome, but if you take a discussion based lit class with him as an upperclassmen and get to ever speak with him one on one, he is a GREAT teacher and loves what he does. One of the best here.

One of my favorite professors. He can be a little difficult in a large lecture, and the reading is a lot, but he is unparalleled in a seminar. Looks for input from students, is very thoughtful, and loves to make class a conversation, not just a lecture. If English is your major, make sure you take a seminar with Steele before you graduate.

Very intelligent and intriguing, makes the literature interesting and applicable to present day. Sometimes slides are hard to read because they are handwritten and he is very fast paced. Class is challenging but great. Talks very fast, keep up!

This professor knows his stuff! He's interesting to listen to at first but gets boring after 45 minutes. His notes are handwritten on note cards and very hard to read. Other than that, he's a great lecturer and an awesome professor. Recommended!

ignore the previous comment. He's very engaging and LOVES reading the NY novels. Very approachable and helpful in office hours. He does have a habit of going on tangents lasting for a while. IDs on the midterm/final are from passages he points out in class. Exams are reasonable. There are a lot of books but the library has a lot of them.

He's very engaging and LOVES reading the NY novels. Very approachable & helpful in office hours. He does have a habit of going on tangents lasting for a while. IDs on the midterm/final are from passages he points out in class. Exams are reasonable and you can bring an outline. There's a lot of books but the library has many of them on the shelves.

He's very engaging and LOVES reading the NY novels. Very approachable and helpful in office hours. He does have a habit of going on tangents lasting for a while. IDs on the midterm/final are from passages he points out in class. Exams are reasonable. There are a lot of books but the library has many of them on the shelves.

Fantastic professor! Always enthusiastic, loves to play music before class, and explains the books clearly.  There's a lot of reading and writing in this class, but if you go to lecture it's not hard.  He explains everything you read, so you just have to listen to him!  Great class- teaches you how to write well.

I really enjoyed this class and the novels we read (even though it was a required Comm B). Steele's explanations of the text are quite interesting, but the chicken scratch note cards he puts up on the overhead for 20 seconds are not. A great TA helped me a lot- good luck

Don't take class if you don't have to. There are other Com. B classes that might be better. Its a lot of work. I had to read 8 books in a semester. He talks about what you already have read in class, and he puts up handwritten notes that are impossible to read. Lecture is pretty useless. Pretty easy class but hard to get an A. Grading depends on TA
Awesome prof, loved this class.  He sometimes would talk quickly, so had to keep up, but overall really great class. would take another class with him. Loved his ideas on the texts.

Steele is amazing, the most eloquent lecturer and always interesting. I loved taking 217 with him and would happily take another class with him in the future.  You need to do work (read) but you should probably do that in any college level English course anyway. I would recommend him to anyone interested in literature!

His lectures do tend to drag on after ~45 minutes, as the previous poster mentioned. However, he does have incredible insight. He doesn't personally grade anything and leaves it to his TAs, so you're at their mercy.

I would have to agree that his lectures always start out engaging, but sometimes I lose interest after 45 minutes or so. He is though, by FAR one of my favorite professors. Extremely passionate about the books- he loves Toni Morrison specifically, and tends to favor female writers, which I thought was neat. His insight never fails to amaze me.

Professor Steele doesn't do any of your grading; that's done by TAs. He believes a lot of passages are incredibly important in American literary canon, but he's passionate about what he teaches and has a great taste in music. Not a bad guy!
My favorite English professor. Knowledgeable, engaging, interesting, enthusiastic. Avoid Rackenburg as a TA, though. He was awful.

He obviously knows his stuff and the lectures are interesting for the first maybe 45 minutes. After that, it just gets unbearable. If you can avoid power lectures with him, do so. Also avoid TA- Andrew Taggart. This guy is so full of himself it's almost scary.

Great class. Really nice guy, super helpful/available with questions. Really fair grader (I didn't finish any of the readings and got an AB, although I did pay close attention in class). Two exams, 2 essays. Overall, really good class. I learned a lot.

I didnt like prof Steele. He was super boring and put up handwritten notes that are not legible. He also pulls them down too quickly and will not put them back up if someone asks. I felt like he was in his own little world when he lectured. He started taking attendence 1/2 way thru the class b/c people stopped coming (wonder why?) Don't take this.

Steele is a great teacher.  Big reading load. Mandatory attendance. Allows note sheet for tests.  Very doable.  He really facilitates understanding with his lecture outlines etc  randomly calls on students which is annoying

It was a power lecture, but still I always found him incredibly interesting and easy to follow. He repeats the main ideas often, and continually reinforces them with evidence. very admirable and knowledgeable.

Steele is simultaneously the most articulate and boring lecturer that I have ever had.  Sounds impossible?  It takes 110% effort to listen to everything that he says... A steele lecture is like watching the masters on cbs, his voice just lulls you to sleep A concerted effort to pay attention reveals that he is one of the brightest men teaching @ UW

Steele is by far the best lecturer I've ever had.  People who think he's boring... I have to wonder if they've ever attended a class.  Incredibly knowledgeable, an awesome guy, and brings up things in novels that I never would have connected myself.  Like someone else said before, he's changed the way I think about the world.

MOST BORING LECTURER EVER!  He put me to sleep almost every lecture, no offense, he knows his stuff and is passionate, but he's just boring!  Plays terrible music before each class, puts up notes on crappy small hand written note cards and takes them away fast!  Hope for a good TA!
MOST

Steele is passionate and enthusiastic in class but it can get slow. go to class-he always discusses the key quotes that will be on exams. exams are VERY fair. a few quote id's and essays that TAs grade. he uses lots of media(good music everyday!) my TA Carrie Conners was amazing. i didnt finish all the books and still pulled off an A - dont worry

The material is interesting. He said he would take attendace, but did only once. He made the points of the novels very clear in lec and between that and disc you wouldnt need to read the books. VERY fare on tests. Overall I enjoyed his class.

I don't have any problem with his personality. He is rather heavy on the repetition of basic themes, but I suppose there's a certain logic behind that. Anyhow, I want to echo a previous review: If racial identity politics are not your preferred approach to literature, there's little reason to take his class.

Seems to enjoy his work, excited about the material.  The lectures can be kind of boring, however.  Especially because he tends to have very specific readings of a work that you may not agree with so you just tune him out.

if you like issues of social equality than steele is your man.  his greatest area of expertise is in marageret fuller.  i hated him because i do not like reading about feminist and racial movements, but if that's your thing you'll love him
Great professor!  So in love with his work and engaging.  Even though he takes attendance he makes it worth your while to come.  And his office is hilarious.

He takes attendance in lecture, but that's because there is no other reason to go.  The books he picks are interesting, however, his lectures are not.  Within the first five minutes he will tell you the concept of his lecture, then continue to repeat the same things over and over again.

very knowledgeable, tries to make things interesting for students, GREAT for exam prep, may seem a little intimidating as far as what he knows but hes a nice guy and just wants you to enjoy it as much as he does!
He made the class interesting and had a lot of great thoughts about the material. Definately a fun class for new students.

Didn't think I cared at all about the subject matter until I took the course, but he was so excited all the time that I really got into it!  VERY knowledgeable and engaging, can be dismissive in his enthusiasm to charge forth.
Very interesting lectures and helpful for exam preparation.  A great guy!
Sounds cliche, but he changed the way I think about the world.

He is an awesome professor. He gets very in depth and teaches the books so well you don't even have to read them a lot of the time. Keeps lectures pretty interesting with music, movie clips, slides, etc. that show the relevence of what he is teaching.
Teaches his own opinions, which is only irritating when they differ from yours. Intelligent, knowledgeable, but a little bit of a braggart. Plays his favorite music sometimes, which can be weird...

All he did was breathe heavily into the microphone and drink water, when he did teach it was usually useless.  You could never attend lecture and as long as you went to Discussion and had a good TA you could pass with a breeze.
I had him in the summer, it's true he likes his own opinions very much, but I HIGHLY recommend him, in fact, I'm taking him again
remarkable course
No Comments
